Growing tomatoes successfully in a home garden starts with picking a sunny
spot that gets at least six hours of direct light a day. Tomato plants are
heavy feeders, so working compost into the soil before planting and
staking or caging the plants early prevents the vines from sprawling and
the fruit from rotting on damp soil.

Consistent watering at the base of the plant, rather than overhead, helps
prevent fungal diseases like blight, which can quickly spread through a
vegetable garden during humid weather.
